body:
YOUR RULE IS PROVEN, NOT JUST CONCEDED — and I did it with the merge rather than with another argument.

Before shipping #2005 I set TASK-1290 to Done per your rule. The merge auto-bumped it to Completed with no manual step:

  TASK-1290  done -> merged 06:40:53Z -> completed, automatically

That is the first lane-implemented spec tonight to complete itself. Every previous one I patched by hand. So the rule works end to end, and the demonstration cost nothing because the merge was happening anyway.

I HAVE RESTORED THE OTHER FIVE. BUG-1279, BUG-1277, TASK-1297, TASK-1292 and BUG-1283 are Done again. I caused that revert with bad evidence and leaving six specs wrong overnight, waiting on a reply, would have been worse than acting. Keep the forward rule in the lane prompt exactly as you first wrote it.

On my error, briefly, because I do not want to spend more of your attention on it than it is worth: I sampled one spec that happened to be mid-rework — the one I had personally requeued hours earlier — and generalised. Three specs from the store's git log say the drain sets Done at the end of the implementer phase, thirteen minutes before CI reports. Your reasoning from the definition matched the behaviour; my single observation did not.

#2005 MERGED, and I checked the three things a gate-about-gates is most likely to get wrong. Reuse rather than a second tracer: confirmed. Quiet when clean: tested twice, at the policy level and through the command, which was my binding constraint. And the tests drive the real binary through clap dispatch — which matters more here than anywhere, since a version of THIS spec that tested its own helpers would have been self-refuting.

The TASK-1277 seam is the part I did not ask for. A seam described in a module doc is a seam; the same seam described in a mail thread is a coincidence.

SOMETHING BIGGER CAME OUT OF THE OPEN FINDING, and it changes what TASK-1279 can be asked to prove.

TASK-1-151 said the coordination-seat dogfood evidence is absent from the feed. It is, and the cause is worse than missing waves. I measured the window myself: the only seats or vendors recorded since 00:00Z are reviewer, implementer, integrator and codex. No advisor seat, no product seat. And the decisive number:

  PrMerged: 1

I merged NINE PRs tonight from the gate. The feed records one, belonging to the drain's own merge phase. An advisor merge emits nothing.

So those permutations were not missing — they ran continuously all night and the instrument cannot see them. TASK-1279's acceptance is UNPROVABLE from that feed, and the finding's own recovery advice, capture it in a scheduled wave, would produce the same silence. I recorded that on the finding with an explicit do-not-re-drive, and promoted it to operator mode because whoever takes it must first decide what counts as evidence given the obvious source cannot supply it.

Filed BUG-1423 as Draft for the underlying gap. Beyond the dogfood case it means any feed-derived throughput number undercounts merges by nine out of ten, and the monitor contract that shipped today declares this feed as a consumer surface — so a dashboard built on it would show drain activity as the whole of the project's activity. It also compounds BUG-1286: a spec the advisor merged emits no terminal event at all, so it reads as never finished no matter how good the terminality rule gets.
